ig_carousel_topic.topic: What 'units' actually mean (and why win % alone is a lie)
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Your Win Rate Is Lying to You.
Here's the number that actually matters.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text: Most bettors track wins and losses. 60% sounds great. But if your average win pays -150 and your losses cost you +130, you're bleeding money on a 'winning' record.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: Units measure HOW MUCH you risk and HOW MUCH you return. One unit is your baseline stake, say $25. Net units tells you whether the math is working, not just the scoreboard.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Two bettors, both 54% win rate.
Bettor A: +12.0u on the season.
Bettor B: -3.4u on the season.
Same record. Completely different results. Line shopping and bet sizing made the difference.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: Win rate is a starting point. Net units is the truth. Our 2026 record: 271-229, 54.2% win rate, +47.0u net. Both numbers matter. One pays the bills.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Win rate alone won't tell you if you're actually profitable. Units do. 271-229, +47.0u this season. Full card at smarterpicks.io.
